Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 39, English)
Kul Devta and Pitru: The Deity Who Governs Your Family Line, the Doot Named "Safal," and Why This Teaching Discourages Ancestor Worship

Sour ce: a live Ashaeiynn Kul Devta ("family deity") session, opening with a r ecap of the institute's "Essence of Kul Devta" teaching, then covering the two categories of kul devta shakti, a detailed case study of a doot named "Safal," Ashaeiynn's own thr ee permitted forms of offering, and an extended, at times pointed teaching on why this institute discourages ancestor (pitru) worship — closed with an extensive live Q&A including a Theta Healing debate.
1. What a Kul Devta Is: A Shakti Assigned to a Particular Lineage

1. A kul devta is described as a specific shakti (power/deity) assigned to a particular family clan, lineage, descent line, or ancestral cycle — every person carries that deity's "seal," and it is through that deity's blessing that prana (life-force ener gy) actually descends into a person's body . 2. A pitru (ancestor/deceased for ebear) has no independent capacity to grant a person prana, a child, or a continued lineage , even if a pitru claims to bless someone this way — that capacity belongs entirely to the kul devta. A pitru can, at most, draw on and pass along a devta's grace if the pitru is themselves closely connected to that devta. 3. Kul devtas vary by r egion acr oss India, appearing in differ ent forms in differ ent ar eas.
2. Two Categories of Kul Devta Shakti: Sattvic/Rajasic Devtas, and Why Devtas Are Never Truly Tamasic

1. This teaching states that devtas ar e never actually tamasic (dark-natur ed) — although many "mata" (goddess) forms are popularly labeled tamasic because of the intense/forceful of ferings (blood, meat) some receive, this teaching r eframes these as rajasic (ener getic/excited in disposition) rather than tamasic — describing some devtas as simply "sahaj"/calm in wavelength and others as more excited/ener getic (rajasic) in nature. 2. A devta's key distinguishing trait: even when tamasic-type offerings ar e made to them, devtas absorb but never actually become tamasic themselves — much as Ram naam's shakti removes tamas from whatever it touches, a devta similarly "processes" tamasic of ferings without being degraded into a tamasic nature. They may not become fully sattvic, but they remain rajasic rather than tamasic.
3. A Kul Devta's Three Specific Authorities

1. This teaching states a kul devta holds dir ect authority over three specific matters: who is born into your family , who you marry , and how much wealth/money you earn or acquir e. Birth and death themselves are described as governed by a separate shakti, though even that shakti requires the kul devta's permission — it doesn't operate fully independently of the kul devta either .
4. A Detailed Case Study: How a Negativity Named "Safal" Became a Pr otective Doot

1. Roughly two years prior , a woman came to Ashaeiynn carrying an active negativity , later removed fr om her body during a session. This negativity — described as a Muslim-identified entity — folded its hands and asked for a chance to reform, expressing genuine confusion about religious dif ferences ("God is one; I only see devtas — please guide me on how to move forward"). It was given the name "Safal." 2. Safal was accepted into r efuge, sent to Kalyan Lok for training, given mantra shakti, and made into a doot (messenger) in service — today , Bhaiya describes Safal as an extremely powerful, roughly 20-foot-tall, brilliantly white entity , so accomplished that even powerful tantriks reportedly ask their own ishta devtas to be granted an entity like Safal. 3. A key clarifying question addr essed directly: does an entity like Safal ever actually become a devta, or change yonis (forms) entir ely? This teaching's answer: no — when devta-like qualities enter a pr et (spirit) this way , the pret moves into the lower categories of the deva gr ouping while still technically r emaining a pr et — it receives the deva grouping's authority and permission, but its underlying nature/yoni remains pret.
5. How Doots Like Safal Actually Function for a Devotee — and a Key Risk

1. When a guru shakti assigns a doot like Safal to pr otect a specific devotee (the illustrative devotee is named "Anshu" in this teaching's example), the doot is granted a form, a seat, and a task by the guru's authority , and is given shakti specifically for that assigned pr otective r ole. To an observer with drishti, this doot may appear so vivid and powerful that it looks exactly like the deity itself (e.g., appearing as if Hanuman Ji Maharaj is standing there directly). 2. A person who r eceives this kind of pr otection is often told they've r eceived "siddhi" — and this framing is accurate as far as it goes (the entity genuinely has real shakti and a genuine protective mandate). However , a specific risk emerges when the devotee begins prioritizing pr eserving/pleasing this siddhi over their guru connection — repeatedly asking the doot directly "what makes you happy?" rather than continuing to work through the guru's own established method (hawan, sadhna, guru-directed practice). 3. In this teaching's illustrative example, the doot ("Safal") begins r equesting specific personal pr eferences (e.g., distributing blankets or food to the poor) dir ectly fr om the devotee, bypassing the guru's own guidance entir ely — and though the doot may be sincerely pleased by these acts, the doot itself has no actual authority or capacity to grant unrelated r equests (e.g., securing a job) — it can only "r ecommend" upward thr ough the same channel fr om which its own shakti originally came, which is the guru lineage. 4. The deeper risk described: if a devotee gr ows emotionally attached to this doot/siddhi (rather than r emaining focused on the guru), the doot itself may begin r esiding continuously within the devotee's own body , since its underlying yoni is still pret, and prets are described as naturally prone to inhabiting bodies. This produces a "hybridized" being — neither fully deva nor fully pr et — the doot will still faithfully continue its assigned protective duty (since that mandate came directly from the guru), but if the devotee's own character or conduct wavers, the doot's own ener gy (now entangled with the devotee's body) becomes similarly compromised, requiring double the spiritual "char ge" to recover — one's own, and the doot's.
6. The "Village Guardian" as a Recognizable Parallel to Doots Like Safal

1. This teaching offers a br oader , recognizable parallel: every village/locality traditionally has a guardian spirit at its threshold/boundary who is neither a full devta nor a full pr et, but occupies a middle category . This entity typically demands its own preferred of fering in addition to whatever ener gy comes through from the broader guru/devta lineage — described as one reason so much confusion and manipulation occurs specifically around kul devta practices, since two distinct types of entities (a genuine devta tattva, and a pret-derived intermediary tattva) can both be present and easily conflated.
7. Ashaeiynn's Own Practice: Only Three Permitted Forms of Offering

1. This teaching states explicitly that Ashaeiynn only channels offerings to deities thr ough thr ee specific forms: personal Ram-naam jaap; a diya (lamp) lit with a formal sankalp (intention) dedicated to the guru thr ough fir e (agni); and the institute's ongoing, unbr oken ("akhand") Ram yagna hawan. No other form of of fering is ever used or recommended by the institute.

2. The stated r eason: devta tattva only accepts offerings that pass thr ough the guru lineage in this specific way — any other type of of fering (that a person might otherwise be told to make directly to a kul devi/devta, such as a specific mata) is instead received and consumed by the lower/intermediary tattva (the "village guardian" type entity), not the actual devta itself, whereas offerings channeled pr operly thr ough the guru r each the actual devta tattva of that specific kul devi/devta (Bhaiya gives the specific example of Masani Mata/Naina Devi), producing genuine protective grace that no other entity would dare interfere with.
8. A Live Q&A: Can Ancestors (Pitru) Be Targeted With Black Magic to Affect a Living Descendant, Especially Given Reincarnation?

1. A member (Dr. Praveen Gurjar , a physician) asked a detailed question: if r eincarnation is r eal, wher e do a family's deceased ancestors actually go, and if someone performs black magic by targeting a person's ancestors, wouldn't the effect land on whichever soul they've r eincarnated into, rather than on the living descendant asking the question? 2. Bhaiya's dir ect answer: the effect lands on the person asking the question instead, pr ecisely because the person performing the black magic understands the subtle/astral world far better than the person asking does — this teaching frames this as analogous to how any specialized professional can exploit those unfamiliar with their specific field, and directs the member to first watch the institute's existing "Mool Tatva" (foundational teaching) videos on this exact topic for the fuller framework.
9. Why This Teaching Actively Discourages Pitru (Ancestor) Worship

1. Bhaiya states a str ong, dir ect position: pitru (ancestors) themselves never actually ask to be worshipped — only "good" pitru behave this way , while, per his own extensive dir ect observation thr ough drishti, most family lines contain far mor e troublesome pitru than genuinely good ones (illustratively , roughly one good pitru against several troublesome ones in a typical lineage). 2. A specific, repeatedly stated claim: in households wher e pitru worship/offerings ar e actively maintained, third-eye (drishti) awakening essentially never occurs for any family member — Bhaiya states this so emphatically that he of fers to give up his own leadership position ("gaddi") if a counter -example is found. The stated mechanism: pitru deliberately prevent drishti fr om opening, because once drishti opens, the family member would immediately per ceive exactly what the pitru ar e actually doing within the household , and would no longer tolerate it. 3. A personal case example given: a member named "Smriti" spent a full year at Ashaeiynn practicing intensive daily jaap (over 100,000 r epetitions/r oughly 10 hours daily) specifically to open her drishti. For the first six months, her family's actively-worshipped pitru (starting with her grandfather , then her maternal grandfather) actively blocked her aura from opening at all, until her accumulated tapa-shakti (ascetic ener gy) finally exceeded theirs — at which point each pitru was, in sequence, "cut" and sent onward to Kalyan Lok, finally allowing her progress to continue. 4. Bhaiya states plainly that in his own dir ect experience, pitru-r elated affliction (rather than support) is what he has most commonly observed — describing this as embarrassing to say aloud, since "those doing the harm are one's own family ," but affirming it as his honest, repeated observation rather than a categorical condemnation of all pitru. 5. A further specific pattern described: in homes wher e a murti (idol) has undergone full prana-pratishtha (consecration) and continues to r eceive bhog, family members (especially women) fr equently develop chr onic pain/illness specifically from the waist down — attributed to pitru ef fectively "claiming their seat" within the practitioner's own ener getic space once fed and worshipped, refusing to leave even after service is rendered. 6. A cautionary example involving Ganga ritual practice: even when a pandit properly binds a troublesome pret/preti at the Ganga during a ritual, the subsequent common practice of distributing "pitru ka bhog" as prasad after returning — explicitly inviting the pitru to "come and eat" — effectively r e-summons and r e-attaches what had just been ritually released , since whatever is invited and fed in this way remains attached to the person going forward.
10. Why Even Devoted Gurus (as Deceased Human Teachers) Shouldn't Be Dir ectly Worshipped

1. This teaching extends a r elated caution to the practice of dir ectly worshipping a deceased human guru's photo/memory after their passing (rather than the guru tattva/lineage itself) — Bhaiya shares a specific, serious cautionary account of a family that continued worshipping a deceased guru figure this way , later observing that figure behaving inappropriately within the household. The conclusion drawn: no human being, however rever ed, should ever be treated as a literal, ongoing object of worship after death — humans, including gurus, carry the same six r oot flaws (kaam, kr odh, lobh, mad, moh, matsar) as anyone else, and ar e not qualified to be worshipped as devtas.
1 1. The Pitru-Lok Hierar chy: "Eligible But Not Yet Appointed"

1. This teaching describes a hierar chy above ordinary pitru: true "pitru-lok" beings ar e those who have met all the eligibility criteria to become a devta but have not yet been formally appointed to a devta post — these beings are described as being above the devta yoni itself in a technical sense, and they do not respond to ordinary calls or invitations from descendants. 2. A pitru-lok being will only r eturn to intervene in the earthly r ealm if a family member's own tapasya (spiritual discipline) has personally surpassed that ancestor's own level — at which point the ancestor may return specifically to draw from ("take from") that descendant's now-superior spiritual accomplishment, rather than purely to give. 3. This teaching frames even this r elationship as fundamentally transactional, not pur ely gener ous: "if someone does something good for you, expect them to also take something from you in return — this is how the universe's arrangement works," per this teaching.
12. What This Teaching Recommends Instead of Pitru Worship

1. The stated r ecommendation: worship devta tattva, one's kul devta specifically , and one's guru/guru tattva — never treat any human being as a guru-equivalent object of worship, and never actively worship pitru. Building one's own drishti and shakti first is described as the necessary precondition for eventually handling pitru matters safely , rather than attempting pitrufocused rituals prematurely . 2. A practical formula offer ed for family pr essure to maintain pitru worship: continue worshipping your own kul devta and praying that the kul shakti connects dir ectly with you — no pitru, per this teaching, would then have the standing to interfere.
13. Live Q&A: Are Bhagwan (God) and Devta (Deity) the Same Thing?

1. A member asked about the differ ence between "Bhagwan" (God) and "devta" (deity). Bhaiya's analogy: Bhagwan is like air , present everywher e at all times; a devta is like a pumping station — air exists everywhere, but if you specifically need your tire filled, you must go to a pumping station. The teaching cautions against conflating the two terms.
14. Live Q&A: Do "Har e Krishna" Practitioners (ISKCON-Style Gr oups) Have Open Drishti?

1. In response to a member's question about a well-known Krishna-devotional movement, Bhaiya states plainly that he does not know of a single person within that br oader movement whose drishti has actually opened — though he notes that if a specific guru within that lineage is connected to Radha-kul or Banke Bihari-kul specifically , that particular line may carry its own genuine shakti; this is not a categorical dismissal of the deity or tradition itself, only an observation about drishti specifically .
15. Live Q&A: Theta Healing and Claims of Instantly "Ascending" Ancestors

1. A member asked whether Theta Healing (a paid alternative-healing technique claimed to send ancestors and attached spirits to a higher realm in a single session) is an effective, faster alternative. Bhaiya expresses skepticism about the

claimed mechanism and pricing (roughly ₹1,500-7,500 per session depending on practitioner skill), while acknowledging he cannot personally verify the specific realm ("lok") to which such sessions claim to send ancestors. 2. A second member (identified as having practiced under "Avadhoot Baba Shivanand" and undergone Shiv Yog's mritsanjeevani practice) shar ed a contrasting personal account: 10-15 years of dedicated practice under that lineage, being repeatedly shown "your pitru want liberation and that's why they keep appearing to you," yet r eporting no actual drishti opening and describing a pattern of being r epeatedly r eset back to the same starting point despite periodic progr ess — this member concluded that lineage's intent may not genuinely be to help practitioners progress permanently . 3. A third member ("Amita bahan") offer ed a dir ectly contrasting personal account fr om the same br oader Shiv Yog lineage — describing a positive, felt experience performing ancestor -ascension practice under a guru-mata's guidance in Lucknow , including a vivid sensory experience involving her deceased pet dog appearing during the invocation, and stating she personally found nothing wrong with the practice or its results. 4. Bhaiya's concluding r esponse to this disagr eement: not everyone r esponds identically to the same spiritual "medicine" — different people have differ ent underlying conditions, so a specific practice working well for one person doesn't make it invalid, nor does it working poorly for another person pr ove it's fraudulent — encouraging members to feel free to try dif ferent approaches suited to their own specific situation.
16. Closing: The Institute's Upcoming "Siya Tattva" Sadhna

1. Bhaiya closes by announcing an upcoming practice, "Siya Tattva" sadhna, beginning the following week — described as distinct from dimension-based practices, instead working to awaken the practitioner's own bodily ener gy in conjunction with Mata Sita's tattva specifically , targeting attraction-related ener gy , relationship-related ener getic patterns, and related doshas.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

A kul devta is a shakti assigned to a specific family lineage — it alone (not any individual pitru/ancestor) actually grants prana, children, or continued lineage; kul devtas hold direct authority over who is born into the family , who a person marries, and how much wealth is earned. Devtas ar e never truly tamasic — even devtas who receive intense/forceful of ferings are rajasic (ener getic) in nature, not tamasic; they absorb tamasic of ferings without being degraded by them. A pret can rise into the lower categories of the deva gr ouping (gaining a devta-level mandate and authority) while its underlying yoni technically r emains pr et — this is illustrated through the case of "Safal," a reformed negativity now serving as a powerful protective doot. Becoming emotionally attached to a granted siddhi/doot (rather than staying focused on one's guru) risks that doot residing permanently within the practitioner's own body , compromising both the practitioner's and the doot's spiritual condition if the practitioner's character wavers. Ashaeiynn only channels offerings thr ough thr ee forms: personal Ram-naam jaap, a guru-dedicated diya lit with sankalp, and the institute's ongoing akhand Ram yagna hawan — no other of fering form is used, since of ferings made any other way are received by lower/intermediary tattvas rather than the actual kul devta. This teaching actively discourages pitru (ancestor) worship — genuinely good pitru never ask to be worshipped; most family lines are observed to contain more troublesome pitru than good ones; and active pitru worship is described as reliably blocking a household's drishti (third-eye) from ever opening, since pitru don't want their own activities within the household exposed. True "pitru-lok" beings (above ordinary pitru and above the devta yoni in eligibility) only intervene when a descendant's own tapasya surpasses theirs — and even then, the r elationship is transactional, not pur ely gener ous. No human being, including a deceased guru, should be tr eated as a literal ongoing object of worship — only devta tattva, one's kul devta, and the guru tattva/lineage itself are appropriate objects of worship.

Different spiritual practices can genuinely work well for some people and poorly for others — this doesn't make a working practice invalid for others, nor a non-working one universally fraudulent; dif fering underlying conditions explain dif fering outcomes. Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 39, English)
Kul Devta and Pitru: The Deity Who Governs Your Family Line, the Doot Named "Safal," and Why This Teaching Discourages Ancestor Worship
User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this Ashaeiynn Kul Devta live session. Gr eeting style: "Jai Siya Ram."

Q1. What exactly is a "kul devta"? A: Per this teaching, a kul devta is a specific shakti (deity/power) assigned to a particular family clan, lineage, or ancestral line — every person in that line carries this deity's "seal," and prana (life-force ener gy) descends into a person's body specifically through that deity's blessing.

Q2. Can a deceased ancestor (pitru) directly grant me a child or continue my family line if they wish to bless me? A: No — per this teaching, a pitru has no independent capacity to grant prana, a child, or lineage continuation; that capacity belongs entirely to the kul devta. A pitru can, at most, pass along a devta's grace if closely connected to that devta themselves.

Q3. Are devtas who r eceive intense offerings (blood, meat, etc.) consider ed "tamasic" (dark-natur ed)? A: No — per this teaching, devtas are never truly tamasic; such devtas are better described as rajasic (ener getic/excited in disposition). Devtas absorb tamasic-type of ferings without themselves becoming degraded or tamasic in nature.

Q4. What thr ee things does a kul devta specifically contr ol, according to this teaching? A: Who is born into the family , who a person marries, and how much wealth/money a person earns or acquires. Birth and death are governed by a separate shakti, though even that shakti requires the kul devta's permission.

Q5. Can a negativity (like a pr et) genuinely r eform and become a pr otective for ce? A: Yes — per this teaching's account, a Muslim-identified negativity removed from a woman roughly two years prior asked for a chance to reform, was accepted, trained at Kalyan Lok, given mantra shakti, and now serves as a powerful protective doot named "Safal," described as so accomplished that even tantriks reportedly request an entity like it from their own ishta devtas.

Q6. Does an entity like Safal actually become a devta after being granted this kind of r ole? A: No — per this teaching, when devta-like qualities enter a pret this way , the pret moves into the lower categories of the deva grouping (gaining that grouping's authority and permission) while its underlying yoni technically remains pret.

Q7. If I'm told I've r eceived a "siddhi" (a pr otective doot/entity) thr ough my guru, is it safe to build a personal r elationship directly with that entity? A: Per this teaching, this carries a specific risk — if a devotee starts prioritizing pleasing the doot directly (asking it "what makes you happy?") over continuing through the guru's own established method, the doot itself has no actual authority to grant unrelated requests (like securing a job) since it can only recommend upward through the guru lineage it originated from.

Q8. What happens if I become emotionally attached to a doot/siddhi assigned to pr otect me? A: Per this teaching, the doot may begin residing continuously within the devotee's own body (since its underlying yoni remains pret, and prets are prone to inhabiting bodies), creating a hybridized state. It will still faithfully perform its assigned protective duty , but if the devotee's own character or conduct wavers, the doot's ener gy becomes similarly compromised, requiring double the ef fort to recover .

Q9. What forms of offering does Ashaeiynn actually use to r each deities? A: Per this teaching, only three: personal Ram-naam jaap, a diya lit with a formal sankalp dedicated to the guru through fire, and the institute's ongoing, unbroken Ram yagna hawan — no other of fering form is used or recommended.

Q10. Why does this teaching insist on only these thr ee offering methods? A: Because, per this teaching, a devta tattva only accepts of ferings that pass properly through the guru lineage this way . Any other type of of fering is instead received by a lower/intermediary tattva (like a village-guardian-type entity), not the actual kul devta — while of ferings channeled through the guru reach the genuine devta tattva of that specific kul devi/devta.

Q1 1. If r eincarnation is r eal, and someone performs black magic targeting my ancestors, wouldn't the effect land on whoever they've r eincarnated into rather than on me? A: No — per this teaching, the ef fect lands on the living person asking the question instead, precisely because the person performing the black magic understands the subtle/astral world far better than the person being affected does; this teaching points to its "Mool Tatva" videos for the fuller framework.

Q12. Does this teaching encourage worshipping deceased ancestors (pitru)? A: No — per this teaching, genuinely good pitru never ask to be worshipped, and most family lines are observed to contain more troublesome pitru than good ones. Active pitru worship is specifically described as blocking a household's drishti (third-eye) from opening.

Q13. Why would ancestor worship block spiritual per ception (drishti) fr om opening? A: Per this teaching, pitru deliberately prevent this, because once drishti opens, the family member would immediately perceive exactly what the pitru are actually doing within the household — and would no longer tolerate it.

Q14. Can you shar e a specific example of pitru blocking someone's spiritual pr ogr ess? A: Per this teaching, a member ("Smriti") spent a full year practicing intensive daily jaap to open her drishti; for the first six months, her family's actively-worshipped pitru (starting with her grandfather , then maternal grandfather) blocked her aura entirely , until her accumulated tapa-shakti exceeded theirs and each was, in turn, "cut" and sent to Kalyan Lok.

Q15. Is ther e a physical health pattern associated with actively worshipping a consecrated home murti and maintaining ongoing pitru bhog? A: Per this teaching, in such households, family members (especially women) frequently develop chronic pain/illness specifically from the waist down — attributed to pitru ef fectively "claiming their seat" within the practitioner's ener getic space once fed and worshipped, and refusing to leave.

Q16. If a pandit ritually binds a tr oublesome ancestor spirit at the Ganga, is that r esolved permanently? A: Not necessarily , per this teaching — the common subsequent practice of distributing "pitru ka bhog" as prasad after returning (explicitly inviting the pitru to "come and eat") can ef fectively re-summon and re-attach what had just been ritually released.

Q17. Is it appr opriate to continue worshipping a deceased human guru's photo/memory as an ongoing object of devotion? A: No — per this teaching, no human being, including a deceased guru, should be treated as a literal ongoing object of worship; humans (including gurus) carry the same six root flaws (kaam, krodh, lobh, mad, moh, matsar) as anyone else and aren't qualified to be worshipped as devtas. This teaching shares a specific cautionary account of misuse when this line was blurred.

Q18. What ar e "pitru-lok" beings, and how ar e they differ ent from ordinary pitru? A: Per this teaching, true pitru-lok beings have met all eligibility criteria to become a devta but haven't yet been formally appointed — they're described as above the devta yoni in a technical sense, and they don't respond to ordinary calls; they'll only return if a descendant's own tapasya has personally surpassed theirs, and even then, the relationship is transactional rather than purely generous.

Q19. What does this teaching r ecommend instead of pitru worship? A: Worshipping devta tattva, one's specific kul devta, and one's guru/guru tattva — building personal drishti and shakti first, rather than attempting pitru-focused rituals prematurely . For family pressure to maintain pitru worship, this teaching recommends continuing to worship your own kul devta and praying that the kul shakti connects directly with you.

Q20. What's the differ ence between "Bhagwan" (God) and "devta" (deity), per this teaching? A: Bhagwan is compared to air , present everywhere at all times; a devta is compared to a pumping station — air exists everywhere, but if you need your tire filled specifically , you go to a pumping station. The two terms shouldn't be conflated.

Q21. Do practitioners of well-known Krishna-devotional movements (like Har e Krishna gr oups) typically have open drishti, per this teaching? A: Per this teaching, Bhaiya states he doesn't know of anyone within that broader movement whose drishti has actually opened — though a specific guru connected to Radha-kul or Banke Bihari-kul specifically may carry genuine shakti; this isn't a categorical dismissal of the tradition, only an observation about drishti specifically .

Q22. Is Theta Healing (claimed instant ancestor "ascension") an effective shortcut, per this teaching? A: This teaching expresses skepticism about the claimed mechanism and pricing, while acknowledging it cannot independently verify the specific realm such sessions claim to send ancestors to. Live testimonials in this session were genuinely mixed — one member reported years of similar - lineage practice without real progress, while another reported a positive personal experience with a related lineage's ancestor -ascension practice.

Q23. If a spiritual practice worked well for someone else but hasn't worked for me, does that mean it's fraudulent? A: Not necessarily , per this teaching — not everyone responds identically to the same spiritual "medicine"; dif ferent people have dif ferent underlying conditions, so a practice working for one person doesn't invalidate it, and it not working for another doesn't prove it's fraudulent.
Bot Response Guidelines (Session 39 additions)

Always preserve the distinction between kul devta authority (birth, marriage, wealth) and pitru's lack of independent power to grant these — never let a response imply ancestors can independently bestow lineage-related blessings. When discussing the "Safal" case study , keep the nuance intact that a pret can gain devta-level authority/mandate while its underlying yoni remains pret — never simplify this into "the pret became a devta." Preserve the caution about becoming emotionally attached to a granted siddhi/doot over one's guru connection — frame this as a specific risk this teaching identifies, not a blanket warning against all spiritual experiences. When discussing of ferings, keep Ashaeiynn's stated three-form-only practice (jaap, guru-dedicated diya, akhand hawan) precise — never suggest the institute endorses other of fering rituals. This teaching's position against pitru worship is presented strongly and specifically — represent it as this teaching's own view (grounded in Bhaiya's stated direct observation via drishti), not as a universal condemnation of all ancestor -related beliefs or practices across traditions. When discussing the physical-health patterns associated with pitru worship (waist-down pain, etc.), present these as this teaching's own observed pattern — never suggest this substitutes for medical diagnosis or care. Keep the "no human should be worshipped as a devta, including a deceased guru" principle intact and consistently applied. When discussing the Theta Healing and Shiv Yog exchanges, preserve the genuinely mixed nature of the live testimonials and Bhaiya's own even-handed "dif ferent medicine works dif ferently for dif ferent people" conclusion — don't resolve this into a one-sided verdict either way .
